C1.quote: the nature of the language to be designed (non-strict, purely functional)
C1.statement: L is non-strict, purely functional with lazy (call-by-need) evaluation as its defining core, embracing both the power (infinite structures, elegant combinators) and the cost (unpredictable space and evaluation order) that laziness brings.

C2.quote: The Haskell Committee was resolute in its decision to keep the language pure—meaning no side effects— so the design of the I/O system was an important issue.
C2.statement: Purity, meaning no side effects, is held to firmly, which makes controlled handling of effects (I/O, state, exceptions) through monads the central design achievement and L's conscious long-term bet.

C3.quote: Aside from laziness, type classes are undoubtedly Haskell's most distinctive feature.
C3.statement: Type classes, with their generalisations to higher kinds (constructor classes), multi-parameter classes, and functional dependencies, are L's most distinctive feature after laziness and the principled solution to overloading.

C4.quote: Miranda added strong polymorphic typing and type inference, ideas that had proven very successful in ML.
C4.statement: L has strong static polymorphic typing with Hindley-Milner inference, inherited from ML via Miranda and extended anarchically into a laboratory for type-system research.

C5.quote: Hope, the language that introduced algebraic data types
C5.statement: Algebraic data types defined as a sum of products, together with top-to-bottom left-to-right pattern matching, are fundamental to the language and its readability.

C6.quote: Despite this, the Haskell Committee worked very hard...on designing (and arguing about) the syntax of Haskell.
C6.statement: Syntax was treated as the user interface and worked very hard: layout/offside rule, infix operators and sections, currying by juxtaposition, few keywords, aiming for programs that look like mathematics and read nicely.

C7.quote: It was decided that a committee should be formed to design such a language
C7.statement: L was built by committee as a conservative common standard embodying consensus (ideally tried-and-true ideas) to unite the scattered lazy-functional community, with stability (L 98) and a growing community taken as both goal and measure of success.
